title: Aeneas: restoration, dating, and provenance of Latin inscriptions
summary: The model restores texts with 73% top-20 accuracy for gaps up to ten characters (58% when length is unknown), attributes provenance with 72% accuracy across 62 Roman provinces, and dates inscriptions within 13 years; it was trained on over 176,000 inscriptions. In a study with 23 historians on 60 inscriptions, results were best when parallels and predictions were used together. Published in Nature.

evidence.tested: Corpus of 176,861 Latin inscriptions. Aeneas: 72% geographical accuracy over 62 provinces; dating within 13 years on average; restoration character error rate 40.5% with known length. 23 historians on 60 inscriptions, solo versus with Aeneas parallels and predictions.
evidence.unknown: The paper notes a small dataset, survival bias, only about 5% of inscriptions with images, and weaker results where data are scarce. Training data include earlier editors' restorations. Other languages are suggested, not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Aeneas restored text, attributed provinces, estimated dates and retrieved parallels; historians evaluated outputs and combined them with their own knowledge.
